Week 45 Appendix: Rhetoric Becomes Apparatus

A president's call to execute dissenting lawmakers turned into Pentagon and FBI action this week, even as courts pushed back on parallel abuses of power.

This week showed a president openly demanding execution and imprisonment of political opponents, military threats against a sitting senator, and a Justice Department run as an instrument of personal retribution, even as courts, in several notable instances, pushed back and forced retreats. The dominant story is escalating governing-by-retaliation: Trump's public order to prosecute enemies, DOJ investigations of Schiff and Cook, Pentagon threats against Senator Kelly, and FBI probes of lawmakers over a video reminding troops of their constitutional duties. Simultaneously, a major foreign-policy scandal emerged: leaked transcripts revealed Trump's envoy coaching Russian officials on manipulating Trump into accepting a Russian-drafted Ukraine 'peace plan,' triggering bipartisan alarm about capture of U.S. foreign policy by an adversary. Courts dismantled several of the administration's illegal prosecutorial actions (Comey/James dismissals, Texas gerrymander blocked), showing judicial resilience even as executive overreach intensified. Immigration enforcement expanded into mass ethnic profiling, family separation, and DC militarization following a shooting, alongside inflammatory presidential rhetoric threatening denaturalization.

Power and Authority

  1. Trump publicly ordered Attorney General Bondi to prosecute perceived enemies including Comey, James, and Schiff: A sitting president's public order to prosecute named political opponents undermines the independence of federal law enforcement from partisan retaliation. (2025-11-22)
  2. Trump demanded arrest and execution of six Democratic lawmakers, calling their video seditious and death-punishable: A president publicly calling for the arrest and execution of elected members of Congress over protected speech is an extraordinary attack on separation of powers and constitutional protections for dissent.   3. Trump threatened to withhold federal funding from New York City over Mamdani's election, then reversed and met cordially with him: The reversal of a prior threat to withhold federal funds based on election outcome, without explanation, illustrates unpredictable and potentially coercive use of federal power against local officials.
